takeaways: Global liquidity is diverging as the PBOC implements accommodative measures to stimulate growth, while U.S. Treasury volatility and rising yields force investors to reassess duration risk and capital allocation.

Institutional capital is pivoting toward AI-related physical infrastructure, with firms like Bank of America and Nvidia shifting hardware costs into long-term, third-party financed assets to sustain demand.
China's export-led 'new shock' is driven by structural domestic overcapacity in EVs and tech, forcing firms to seek global markets as domestic consumption remains weak despite policy support.

items.title: China's central bank promises policy support, stronger countercyclical adjustments
bullets: The PBOC is shifting its primary short-term operational target from the seven-day repo rate (DR007) to the overnight repo rate (DR001), reflecting a strategic move to better manage liquidity as overnight transactions now comprise over 90% of the repo market.

Despite global tightening trends, the PBOC plans to introduce incremental policy measures to maintain accommodative financing conditions, signaling a divergence from the hawkish stances currently adopted by the Federal Reserve and other major central banks.
items.reason: Signals significant monetary policy divergence and operational framework shifts in the world's second-largest economy.

items.title: Imported Inflation Hits as PBOC Flags Overseas Rate Hikes: This Cycle's Impact Seen as Relatively Mild
bullets: The PBOC identifies a convergence of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and an AI-driven demand surge for semiconductors and power as primary drivers of current imported inflationary pressures.

Chinese policymakers anticipate that the current global monetary tightening cycle will have a relatively mild impact on the domestic economy compared to previous episodes, despite the hawkish tilt observed in the Federal Reserve's recent policy signals.
items.reason: Provides critical insight into China's assessment of global inflation risks and the potential impact on domestic monetary policy.

items.title: Bank of Lithuania Blocks Lux International Payment System Services
bullets: The Bank of Lithuania has imposed an immediate, broad-based suspension on UAB Lux International Payment System, prohibiting the firm from serving both new and existing customers due to suspected serious AML and counter-terrorist financing deficiencies.

This regulatory intervention is particularly aggressive as it halts all existing financial services rather than just new onboarding, highlighting a tightening of oversight on electronic money institutions within the EU jurisdiction.
items.reason: Highlights increasing regulatory scrutiny and operational risks for fintech and electronic money institutions in the European market.

bullets: SK Hynix has abruptly ceased its bond-buying activities, opting instead to move significant cash reserves into commercial bank deposits, which creates immediate liquidity concerns for the South Korean short-term credit market.

Industry analysts suggest this strategic shift may be intended to prioritize higher shareholder returns, signaling a potential change in corporate capital allocation that could impact broader domestic bond market stability.

items.title: The $30 trillion Treasury market is facing a painful reckoning. How rising yields could squeeze your portfolio. - MarketWatch
bullets: The $30 trillion U.S. Treasury market is experiencing heightened volatility as rising yields exert downward pressure on fixed-income valuations, forcing investors to reassess duration risk in their portfolios.

Persistent yield increases threaten to compress total returns across asset classes, necessitating a defensive posture for investors heavily exposed to interest-rate sensitive debt instruments in the current macroeconomic environment.
items.reason: Systemic risk to the global benchmark asset class.

items.title: PBOC Q2 Monetary Policy Report: H1 GDP Grows 4.7%, Yuan Strengthens 3% vs Dollar, Creates 1 Trillion Yuan Private Enterprise Relending Facility
bullets: The PBOC has launched a 1 trillion yuan private enterprise relending facility to bolster liquidity, alongside a 25 basis point reduction in interest rates for structural monetary policy tools to lower corporate financing costs.

Monetary authorities are refining interest rate control by narrowing the repo operation corridor to 50 basis points and introducing new tools for overseas central banks to manage renminbi liquidity and bond allocations.
items.reason: Significant shift in monetary policy and liquidity support.

items.title: Excess savings are driving the new ‘China shock’
bullets: Unlike the previous export-led growth model, the current 'China shock' is characterized by domestic technological upgrading combined with persistent weak domestic demand, forcing excess production into global markets.

Investors should note that the surge in exports is less about direct government subsidies and more a structural byproduct of high domestic savings and under-consumption, which risks prolonged global trade tensions.
items.reason: Structural shift impacting global trade and investment strategy.

items.title: Forget chatbot training. AI's next big data grab is about learning how humans work.
bullets: Tech giants are shifting from static text-based training to 'reinforcement learning environments,' where AI agents simulate real-world workplace tasks like coding and software navigation to improve autonomous performance.

Google is reportedly in talks to invest over $1.5 billion in the startup Mechanize, while Meta is actively collecting granular user data—including keystrokes and mouse movements—to train models on human workflow patterns.
items.reason: Signals a major pivot in AI development strategy and capital allocation.

items.title: From Apple to Netflix: Why Big Tech is pushing deeper into gaming ecosystem
bullets: Major tech firms including Samsung, Apple, and Netflix are integrating gaming deeper into their hardware and service stacks to increase user retention and justify premium silicon performance.

Apple is increasingly leveraging its proprietary chips to support console-quality gaming, using a unified 'Games' app across iOS and macOS to lock users into its ecosystem and drive hardware upgrade cycles.
items.reason: Highlights a critical strategy for hardware monetization and ecosystem stickiness.

items.title: AI was supposed to destroy jobs. Where’s the carnage?
bullets: Economic data from the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research indicates that unemployment for workers most exposed to AI has risen by only 0.77 percentage points since 2022, trailing the 0.85 percentage-point increase seen in least-exposed sectors.

The lack of mass displacement suggests that AI is currently augmenting rather than replacing labor, mirroring the slow adoption curves of previous technological revolutions and shifting corporate expectations toward requiring AI-specific skills.
items.reason: Challenges the prevailing bearish narrative on AI-driven labor market disruption.

items.title: Advanced Micro Devices vs. Alphabet: Which Artificial Intelligence Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
bullets: AMD demonstrated significant financial momentum in FY 2025 with $34.6 billion in revenue, a 34.3% year-over-year growth rate, and a robust balance sheet featuring a low 0.1x debt-to-equity ratio.

While AMD scales through strategic acquisitions like Taalas and ZT Design, Alphabet maintains a distinct competitive advantage through massive, stable cash flows derived from its dominant digital advertising and cloud infrastructure ecosystems.
items.reason: Provides a comparative fundamental analysis of two key AI supply chain players.

items.title: EVs dominate China’s car market: 5 takeaways from the country's latest auto sales data
bullets: New energy vehicles reached a 65.1% market share of new passenger car sales in July, marking a significant increase from 54% in the same period last year.
Despite the high market penetration, domestic passenger car sales overall plummeted 20.3% in July, with year-to-date EV sales through July declining by 12.5%.
items.reason: Significant shift in market share despite overall sector contraction.

items.title: China's NEV sales rise 23.7% in July, with exports surging 1.5 times, CAAM data shows
bullets: China's NEV exports surged 1.5 times year-on-year to 553,000 units in July, helping to offset weak domestic demand and pushing total vehicle exports above 1 million for the second consecutive month.
NEV sales reached 1,561,000 units in July, accounting for over 60% of total new vehicle sales for the first time, signaling a structural shift toward electrification despite domestic volatility.
items.reason: Export growth is becoming a critical counterbalance to domestic market weakness.

items.title: Bank of America to Deploy $250 Billion to Bolster AI and Energy Infrastructure
bullets: Bank of America is launching a $250 billion 'Critical Infrastructure Finance Initiative' to be deployed over 18 months, specifically targeting data centers, semiconductor facilities, and power generation projects.

The initiative aims to mobilize capital through lending, advisory, and investment transactions to address the massive surge in demand for computing power and energy security, signaling significant institutional support for AI-related physical infrastructure.
items.reason: Major institutional capital commitment to the sector.

items.title: Nvidia found a new way to keep the AI boom funded: your retirement money
bullets: Nvidia is partnering with major alternative asset managers like Apollo, Blackstone, and KKR to create financing platforms that treat AI compute as a long-term infrastructure asset rather than a depreciating hardware expense.

By shifting AI infrastructure financing to third-party institutional investors, Nvidia aims to move capital-intensive data center projects off its customers' balance sheets, potentially sustaining demand for its GPUs despite rising interest rates.
items.reason: Structural shift in how AI infrastructure is financed.

items.title: Firefly Aerospace pushes debut of Alpha Block 2 rocket to the fourth quarter of 2026
bullets: Firefly Aerospace reported a $25.8 million increase in second-quarter R&D costs, primarily driven by production scaling for its Alpha Block 2 rocket and stock-based compensation expenses.
The company has delayed the debut of its Block 2 configuration to Q4 2026, though it claims to have already sold the majority of its 2027 launch manifest to commercial and government customers.
items.reason: Operational delays and rising R&D costs impact the financial outlook for a key private launch provider.

items.title: Vietnam’s VinSpace Signs Deal With Elon Musk’s SpaceX to Launch Satellites in 2027
bullets: VinSpace has contracted with SpaceX for a 2027 Transporter rideshare mission, marking a strategic expansion of Vietnam's domestic aerospace capabilities and satellite manufacturing sector.
The mission will focus on in-house technology demonstrations, signaling a move toward full-stack aerospace operations including satellite design, manufacturing, and downstream data services.
items.reason: Highlights the growing international commercial demand for SpaceX's rideshare program and emerging market space investment.
